texts: Use of an RV-PA conduit may improve outcomes after stage I reconstruction: D.

In the Single Ventricle Reconstruction trial, transplant-free survival at 12 months was better with the RV-PA (Sano) conduit than with a modified Blalock-Taussig shunt, though the advantage faded later.
The conduit avoids diastolic runoff from the aorta, which protects coronary perfusion.
Ten-year survival is now well over 50 percent, interstage home monitoring reduces deaths between stages, and preoperative ECMO or VAD support raises operative mortality.
In the picture, more waterslide hotels than hose hotels stand at their first birthday.
Memory hook: the waterslide beats the hose in the first year.
